correctness.rationale: Walsh autocorrelation inversion is exact; support-direction span follows from nonzero pair differences. A clique in the difference graph of an affinely independent support is a star for sizes five and six; at size four the only triangle alternative duplicates differences and fails the input correlation. Every dependent support through size six is a plane, plane-plus-one, six-of-eight affine flat, plane-plus-two independent outer points, or a full six-point circuit, with direct correlation formulas and rigid reconstruction in the noncircuit cases. The circuit case has fifteen distinct pair differences saturating its four-space and the count 448 per four-flat. C++17 exact exhaustive enumerator agrees for all sizes one through six in a universal five-dimensional test space, and is supplementary to the analytic infinite-family proof.

originality.rationale: The claim is the sharp indexed Fourier-intensity reconstruction threshold and the entire six-point homometric fiber in all Boolean dimensions. Its building blocks (autocorrelation equivalence and 16,6,2 difference sets) are acknowledged prior results. Full-text comparisons with primary phase-retrieval papers show no statement implying the complete threshold and fiber count. Specialized older Boolean homometry enumeration remains a plausible residual risk, rather than being ruled out by failed search.
residual_risks: Older specialized homometric-set or Boolean difference-set classification might indirectly imply the sharp support-five threshold or all translation fibers; Rosenblatt–Seymour full text was not available in this review.
The classical (16,6,2) design construction and its flat Fourier spectrum are prior; novelty is limited to the universal sharp reconstruction and complete ambiguity-fiber classification.

value.rationale: Sharp recoverability threshold for a standard inverse-Fourier observable, valid in every binary dimension. The only loss of injectivity at the smallest threshold is completely described: which supports, which difference subspace, how many translations and nontranslations. This is a naturally motivated inverse problem; the joint classification provides substantially more than the classical existence of a bent six-point difference set.
